chunks: Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Ibn Muskān, from Abd al-Mu'min, from Sābir, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who rents his house where wine is sold; he said, 'Its rent is forbidden.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on renting a house where wine is sold?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) rules that the rent (*ajr*) from a property used for selling wine is forbidden, illustrating the principle of *al-khamr* (wine) as a primary impurity that contaminates associated economic transactions. This ruling underscores the Shia jurisprudential view that the permissibility of income is intrinsically linked to the primary utility of the asset, extending the prohibition of wine consumption to its commercial trade and the revenue generated from it. It serves as a key example of how minor commercial activities are evaluated based on the dominant purpose of the space or item involved.
